rationale: The new SEN-D1 sensor timed out during pairing (120s) despite being brand new, firmware-compatible (v2 protocol, base supports v2/v3), within range, and with ample capacity (5/16). The base station was online with no fault codes and all other devices heartbeating normally, ruling out network/capacity/protocol issues. A peripheral factory reset (15s SYNC hold) followed by a correct pairing sequence resolved it immediately, confirming a stale peripheral binding state rather than a hardware fault.

repair_steps: Instruct the customer to factory reset the new sensor by holding its SYNC button for 15 seconds until the LED flashes white.
Have the customer put the base station into pairing mode via the app (Add Device) and confirm the base station LED is blinking blue.
Guide the customer to hold the sensor's SYNC button for 3 seconds until its LED blinks blue, keeping it within 1 metre of the base station.
Verify the sensor appears in the app and is online.
output.customer_reply: Thanks for your patience. The issue was a stale state on the new sensor. A factory reset and re-pairing resolved it. Your new sensor is now connected and working. If you need further help, let us know!

results.source: manual_base_station#Orphaned binding (device removed in app but still bound in base station)
results.text: If a device is removed in the app while it is offline or out of range, the base station may keep its entry. This orphaned ("ghost") binding still occupies a slot, so the base station can report E-201 although the app lists fewer devices than the limit. Frontline cannot clear it: the app only removes devices it lists, re-pairing does not free the slot, and a base-station factory reset is not allowed. Treat it as a binding-table inconsistency (app and base station disagree) and escalate to FAE, who remove the entry with the backend binding tool. Put the orphaned device id and the bound count (for example 8/8) in the ticket.
